html:
Francisco Solano López was the president of Paraguay from 1862 to 1870, who led the country into the War of the Triple Alliance and died in its last battle.

The son of Carlos Antonio López, he had commanded the army since his youth and lived in Europe, where he met his Irish partner Eliza Lynch. In 1864 he went to war against Brazil, then Argentina, believing a strong Paraguay had to stop its neighbours from swallowing Uruguay.

He fought on long after the war was lost, ordered the execution of many he suspected of treason, and led a dwindling army of old men and boys into the hills. Brazilian troops killed him at Cerro Corá on 1 March 1870. Seen for decades as a tyrant, he was made a national hero under later dictators, including Stroessner. His war is the great trauma of the nation.
sum: Francisco Solano López was the president of Paraguay from 1862 to 1870, who led the country into the War of the Triple Alliance and died in its last battle.
